subject: Behavioral Economics
title: Nudging College Enrollment
description: A quick win: understand Nudging College Enrollment.

hook.text: Accepted students from low-income families often don't show up. They completed the hard part — applying — then melted.

buildup.text: Summer melt: 10-20% of students accepted to college fail to enroll due to complex paperwork and financial steps.

discovery.text: Castleman and Page found that personalized text reminders about deadlines and steps reduced summer melt by 30%.

twist.text: The barrier wasn't motivation or ability. It was friction: confusing FAFSA forms, unclear deadlines, and no guidance.

climax.text: Pre-filling FAFSA forms and assigning advisors who text reminders cost $100 per student and save thousands in lost.

punchline.text: Don't lose students to paperwork. Nudge them through.

quiz.question: What is 'summer melt' in college enrollment?
options: Students dropping out after the first year
Accepted students failing to enroll due to friction and complexity
Students choosing summer jobs over college

details.summary: Nudging college enrollment uses simplified forms, text reminders, and default assistance to increase enrollment among low-income students who have been accepted but fail to enroll. Small barriers like complex forms cause summer melt, where accepted students never show up.
details.whyItMatters: Tens of thousands of low-income students accepted to college fail to enroll each year because of administrative complexity. Targeted nudges like text message reminders and simplified financial aid forms close this gap at a fraction of the cost of.
takeaways: Summer melt causes accepted low-income students to fail to enroll in college
Text reminders and simplified forms significantly increase enrollment rates
Small administrative barriers have outsized effects on educational outcomes

faq.question: What is summer melt and why does it happen?
faq.answer: Summer melt is the phenomenon where students accepted to college do not enroll in the fall. It happens because pre-enrollment tasks such as financial aid verification, housing forms, and orientation registration are complex and overwhelming, especially for first-generation students.

faq.question: How effective are nudges at reducing summer melt?
faq.answer: Text message nudges that provide reminders and guidance about pre-enrollment tasks have been shown to increase enrollment by 3 to 7 percentage points. For low-cost, scalable interventions, these are substantial effects that close equity gaps.
